evidence: junk_imagery: seg0:end/seg1:mid: an alarm-clock emoji sits on the 52% bar and then fills a whole 'each = 5%' grid for 'have used one at least once'. Alarm clocks have nothing to do with teens talking to AI companions.

weakest_scene.visible_evidence: seg2:mid/seg2:end: the labels 'Chose AI over a human for a serious talk 33%' and 'Shared personal info with an AI companion' are drawn on top of each other along one line and clipped at both frame edges. seg2:start is a bare two-circle number card with a garbled '33%'.
weakest_scene.root_cause: The two-pin gap machine puts both long category labels at the same y position with no measured width or collision avoidance. The opening two-circle card has no demonstration at all.
weakest_scene.repair_goal: Show 1 in 3 teens choosing an AI over a person, and 1 in 4 sharing personal info, as a picture made of the subject. For example, a row of teen figures where a third turn toward a phone instead of a person, and a quarter pass a note into a chat bubble. Put each label on its own line, sized by measurement to fit the frame, and have Data act out the choice.
